CONCLUSION: the 238-vs-640 bibliographic gap is an OBSTRUCTION, not an absence. Free-fermion six-vertex partition functions are generically not Lorentzian, so the edge I proposed to build in July does not exist. The Schur case survives because the five-vertex model is NOT homogeneous per row (four weights equal 1) -- its homogeneity comes from the boundary, so the x-degree is a genuine statistic with permutohedral (M-convex) support. That property does not deform. Corroborated from inside HMMS by a mechanism they state (Sec 3.1 footnote): the Newton polytope of any homogeneous strongly log-concave polynomial is necessarily a generalized permutohedron of TYPE A, every edge parallel to some e_i-e_j -- precisely the M-convexity condition my witnesses fail. Positive rigidity result found en route. One-parameter free-fermion deformation off the Schur point (a1=a2=c1=1, b1=x_i, b2=eps, c2=1+eps*x_i): if particles p = rows n then Z_eps = Z_0 * prod_i (1+eps x_i)^n EXACTLY, independent of boundary and of m (verified n=2 m=4,5,6; n=3 m=6,7, all admissible boundaries). If p<n the factorization FAILS (n=3,p=2: no exponent k<=2m works for any boundary). So the deformation is a gauge factor on the diagonal p=n and genuinely deforms only below it -- which is what motivated moving to the homogeneous setting where N(.) is defined.

children.approach: PROVED. Let Gamma_c = {(alpha, c - alpha) : alpha in Z^n} subset Z^{2n} (the graph of an affine reflection) and let S subset Gamma_c be finite nonempty with x-projection A. Then S is M-convex IFF A is an integer box prod_i [l_i, h_i]. Mechanism (Lemma 2.1, 'forced partner'): for u in Gamma_c and p != q, u - e_p + e_q lies in Gamma_c iff q is the partner of p -- the only type-A roots in the direction lattice of Gamma_c are the n opposite pairs +-(e_{x_i} - e_{y_i}), so a 2n-dimensional root system keeps 2n of its 2n(2n-1) roots. Hence the only legal exchange moves one unit between x_p and y_p, giving (T1); descent and ascent claims then force A to contain every lattice point of its bounding box. SIX-VERTEX COROLLARY: supp(Z) is M-convex iff supp(Z) = supp(prod_i P_i) with P_i = sum_{k=l_i}^{h_i} x_i^k y_i^{m-k} -- iff the rows DECOUPLE with no gaps. Corollary (T2): if sum_i alpha_i is constant on A then Z is a monomial.
sources: 1906.09633 Thm 2 and Sec 3.1 footnote (positive control and polytope remark; verified-quote)
